key_insight: A smooth spatial blending of the rotating-frame speed in a modified MRF method removes the artificial jump at the rotating–stationary interface while preserving the low cost of MRF calculations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical middle ground between expensive sliding-interface simulations and less physical classical MRF for predicting propeller–hull interaction and self-propulsion in ship CFD.
method: Scale the reference-frame rotation rate with a spatially varying decay function from 1 near the propeller to 0 at the domain interface.
Derive the modified governing equations and implement them in the FreSCo+ RANS solver.
Verify the formulation against Taylor–Couette flow and apply it to open-water propeller and Japan Bulk Carrier self-propulsion cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate agreement in key propulsion metrics (n, KT, KQ, 1-t, 1-wT, etaR) and shows reduced interface discontinuities and flow artifacts, especially at large MRF fractions.
watch_item: The method still depends on how the decay function and rotating-region extent are chosen, so poor parameterization could leave residual artifacts or weaken the physical fidelity of the interface.
paper_title: A Modified Moving Reference Frame Method for Propeller Resolution
